title: Open WebUI -- T1548 caller-supplied url_idx routes to an admin-disabled Ollama backend
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-54021 (CVSS 6.3 MEDIUM),
affecting Open WebUI prior to 0.9.6.

Several direct, index-addressed Ollama proxy routes accept a
caller-supplied `url_idx` path parameter and use it as a raw index into
the admin-configured `OLLAMA_BASE_URLS` list --
`url = request.app.state.config.OLLAMA_BASE_URLS[url_idx]`, with no
authorization check on the index itself. Access control on these routes
validates only whether the caller may use the requested MODEL, never
which BACKEND the request is routed to -- and an admin-disabled
backend's disabled state is checked only during model discovery, never
re-checked at request time. Any authenticated user can therefore append
an arbitrary `url_idx` to reach an internal, higher-privilege, or
explicitly admin-disabled Ollama backend they were never authorized to
use -- e.g. `POST /ollama/api/chat/3` reaches
`OLLAMA_BASE_URLS[3]` directly even if an admin disabled that backend.

Detection logic flags a request to one of these indexed Ollama proxy
routes carrying a `url_idx` (or equivalent trailing numeric path
segment) whose target backend is outside the caller's model-permitted
set -- the index itself is the vulnerable artifact, since the route's
own authorization never inspects it.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.9.6 (adds `validate_ollama_backend_idx()`,
returning 403 for any non-admin caller-supplied `url_idx` not in the
requested model's allowed URLs).
